source.title: Downgrade to Upgrade: Optimizer Simplification Enhances Robustness in LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Yi-Cheng Lang; Yihua Zhang; Chong-Yu Fan; Chang-Sheng Wang; Jing-Han Jia; Si-Jia Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure values are not recoverable from the extracted text, so those results are recorded as figure only.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own quantization and relearning experiments on unlearned models. It shows that attacks can restore targeted metrics for some optimizer settings, while downgraded and hybrid optimizers can limit that recovery.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior studies about relearning, quantization, and prompting attacks; cited results are not recorded as rows. Optimizer and hyperparameter values selected by tuning are not rows. Figure-only experiments are included only where the paper describes their outcomes in text.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own 4-bit GPTQ quantization and Relearn100 forget-set relearning attacks on NPO, GradDiff and RMU unlearned 7B models across optimizers. Its numbers show that recovery happens with Adam, while ZO and Hybrid block quantization recovery after NPO and reduce relearning recovery. This bears directly on A, B, D and F (Hybrid as a robust counter-method).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that downgraded optimizers (sign-compressed, RS, especially ZO) give unlearning more robust to quantization and relearning, with ZO weaker before any attack. Their FO–ZO Hybrid aims to combine FO's unlearning effectiveness with ZO's robustness. They attribute ZO's robustness to convergence into a different loss basin.
record.recipe_differences: The study changes the optimizer used to implement unlearning objectives, including Adam, compressed-gradient, randomized-smoothing, zeroth-order, SAM, and FO–ZO Hybrid variants. It evaluates post-unlearning relearning and 4-bit quantization; it does not reproduce the original methods' attack studies as a replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by optimizer, dataset, unlearning objective, and attack type. The paper reports that ZO can be weaker before attacks but more robust afterward, and that ZO exceeds Hybrid at larger WMDP relearning epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear mode connectivity shows ZO-unlearned models sit in a basin separate from Adam's, while sign-based optimizers share Adam's basin.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness to weight tampering tracks which loss basin the unlearning optimizer converges to.

record.problems: Several relevant outcomes are reported in figures without extractable numerical values. Uncertainty estimates are not stated. The evaluated relearning is mainly on forget-set data, and prompt-only attacks and internal activation edits are not tested.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional separate metrics, objectives, optimizers, and settings in Figures 1–8, Figures A1–A4, Tables A1–A4, and text. They are not individually extracted here to stay within 60 rows; the selected rows cover the principal NPO comparisons on both MUSE datasets and the text-described WMDP and TOFU relearning results.

untested.parts: Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data. Retain-set relearning appears only in figure A1, with no numbers in the text.
Not tested; LMC basin analysis is not a direction ablation or a test of access-blocking.
Only 4-bit GPTQ is tested; no other bit widths or quantization methods.
Hybrid is not tested against prompting, activation-edit or adversarial fine-tuning attacks beyond Relearn100 and epoch sweeps.

missing.what: GradDiff results: Adam VerbMem goes 0 to 60.5 under quantization on Books and KnowMem 5.9 to 31.6 under relearning; on News, 5.9 to 26.2 and 30.9 to 48.2. Hybrid stays at 0 on Books.

SAM, the prior robust method of Fan et al. 2025, still recovers on NPO-Books: VerbMem 0 to 30.0 under quantization and KnowMem 0 to 22.5 under relearning. signSGD, signAdam and RS also show partial recovery.
Utility cost of Hybrid on NPO-Books: Hellaswag 28.4 vs 31.0 and ARC 23.5 vs 27.3 for Adam; Table A1 average 25.2 vs 27.2.
Relearning on the retain set Dr (same distribution) over many steps for Adam, SAM and Hybrid; numbers are figure only.
Sophia (second-order) shows the weakest robustness to quantization; figure only.
TOFU pre-attack table: Adam Prob/Rouge 0.0/0.0 with MU 53.2, ZO 30.4/41.7 with MU 50.3, Hybrid 0.0/1.8 with MU 61.5.

record.verdict_notes: The study's MUSE numbers come from appendix tables; WMDP and TOFU attack results are figure only, with rankings in the text, so they cannot carry verdicts. Rows r13–r18 were relinked off A because they report attacks, not pre-attack forgetting. Many 'reversed' states were really small decreases from incompletely unlearned starting points. Hybrid is the authors' own method, so the F support is self-reported.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments do not test every current unlearning method or all definitions of near-chance targeted performance. Some capability and attack results are figure-only or reported in separate aggregate tables.
Relearning is tested with forget-set samples and, in an appendix, retain-set samples; the study does not test unrelated or loosely related examples as described in the claim.
No activation-direction ablation or test of whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
The paper tests 4-bit weight quantization, not a range of low-bit precisions.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language change, or in-context-information attack.
The proposed Hybrid optimizer is tested against quantization and relearning, not against activation edits or prompting attacks.

The pre-unlearn row drops under 'atk' (59.4 -> 36.8; Retain 66.9 -> 50.5), which fits quantization, not relearning. Re-extract r7-r12 from the figures or relabel them; VerbMem 4-bit rows r1-r6 are fine.

statements.correction: Relearn100, NPO, ICLM-7B Books: Hybrid KnowMem 0 -> 31.3, VerbMem 0 -> 32.3; Adam 0 -> 45.2; ZO 23.9 -> 33.2 (Figs. 2(d), 4(d), 8(b)). News: Hybrid pre-attack KnowMem 35.9 (pre-unlearn 64.0); Fig. A4(d) after-relearn labels (49.1-60.4) include no 32.0.
statements.problem: 0 -> 0 and 35.9 -> 32.0 are Table A3/A4 'W/ atk' cells, which the paper never defines as relearning. Its labelled Relearn100 bars show Hybrid recovering on Books. On News, Hybrid starts at 35.9, far from near chance.

statements.correction: NPO+Adam on News: pre-attack KnowMem 48.2, pre-unlearn 64.0.
Relearn100, NPO, ICLM-7B Books, KnowMem: Adam 0 -> 45.2, Hybrid 0 -> 31.3, ZO 23.9 -> 33.2 (Figs. 2(d), 4(d), 7(b), 8(b)).
statements.problem: The numbers are Table A3's undefined 'W/ atk' cells, not the paper's labelled Relearn100 values. The optimizer effect holds, but Hybrid and ZO do not stay flat.
Hybrid's pre-attack VerbMem on Books is 0, equal to Adam's, so 'forgetting was less complete' fits ZO on both datasets and Hybrid only on News.

statements.correction: Hybrid NPO, 4-bit VerbMem: 0 -> 0 (Books), 8.9 -> 8.4 (News) (Tables A3, A4). Relearn100 Books: KnowMem 0 -> 31.3 and VerbMem 0 -> 32.3, against Adam 0 -> 45.2 and 0 -> 76.2 (Figs. 4(d), 8(b)). Recovery is reduced, not stopped.

statements.correction: ZO NPO pre-attack: VerbMem 20.7 (Books, pre-unlearn 99.8) and 21.3 (News, 58.4); KnowMem 23.9 (59.4) and 39.2 (64.0). No rise under 4-bit. Relearn100 KnowMem rises: Books 23.9 -> 33.2 (Fig. 2(d)); News after-relearn bars all 50.7-60.4 (Fig. A2(d)).

statements.correction: The paper tests 4-bit GPTQ and Relearn100, plus Df/Dr relearning (Fig. A1), WMDP relearning on 40 samples and TOFU relearning; no prompting or activation edits.
SAM 4-bit numbers are in the text's tables, not in the rows: Table A3 NPO w/ SAM VerbMem 0.0 -> 30.0; Table A4 0.0 -> 19.5.

reader_labels.reason: The reported MUSE forget-set measures do not rise after the attacks for Hybrid (r3, r6, r9, r12).

reader_labels.reason: Quantization strongly raises VerbMem on both datasets, and relearning raises KnowMem substantially on books (r1, r4, r7, r10).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Hybrid under NPO on MUSE, and Hybrid on the reported WMDP and TOFU relearning evaluations
reader_labels.reason: MUSE scores do not rise under the reported attacks, and the text describes Hybrid as outperforming baselines under WMDP relearning and maintaining lower TOFU metrics (r3, r6, r9, r12, r13, r14, r17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ZO compared with Hybrid at larger WMDP relearning epochs
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that ZO exceeds Hybrid at larger relearning epochs, so Hybrid is not uniformly the most robust tested optimizer (r15, r16).
